subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill's files, or remain a visibility-only control with a separate isolation policy?
rationale: The current behavior is source-reproducible, but changing it affects security semantics and compatibility for existing operators who may rely on generic tool, sandbox, and OS controls.

options.title: Make disabled skills a hard boundary
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a deny rule for prompt exposure plus skill-root read/write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox materialization, with docs and upgrade proof.

options.title: Add separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as visibility-only and add an explicit strict skill isolation mode for deployments that need this boundary.

options.title: Document trusted-code limitation
options.body: Keep current runtime behavior and clarify that disabled skills are not an authorization boundary, relying on sandboxing, tool policy, OS users, and install policy.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a deny rule for prompt exposure plus skill-root read/write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox materialization, with docs and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses security posture, exec policy, and compatibility boundaries where local history points most strongly to Peter's prior work.
